summary: František Šohaj was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed his Ph.D. at Charles University by 1848. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Charles University from 1848 to 1859 and held a post at Akademické gymnázium v Praze in 1859.

Franz Altheim was a historian, archaeologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt (1916–1921). He held professorships at Halle (1936), Halle-Wittenberg (~1937–1950), and the Free University of Berlin (1950–1965).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from UC Berkeley, an MA from the Graduate Theological Union, and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago, serving as an instructor at CSU Los Angeles in 1998.

Franz August Schmölders was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at Bonn (~1827–1836) and studied in Paris. He served as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842) and became a professor at the University of Breslau in 1846.

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Werner Thomas, and completed his habilitation at Frankfurt. He held posts at Tübingen, Frankfurt, and served as professor at Hamburg (1966–1971).

Linguist Franz Boas studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Friedrich Ratzel and Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University (~1889–1892), the American Museum of Natural History (1896–1900), and Columbia University (~1896–1942), which he founded.

Franz Bopp worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Antoine-Léonard Chézy, and Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann in Paris and Göttingen. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

Franz Carl Christian Vorländer worked in philosophy and Indology, studying under Franz Bopp, Karl Lachmann, and Friedrich Schleiermacher before earning his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin (PD, 1842) and Marburg (ao. Professor, 1843).

Franz Ferdinand Schwarz was an Indologist, linguist, and historian-archaeologist. He studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz, earning his Ph.D. (~1954–1961) and PD qualification (~1961–1973), and served there as professor from 1976.

Franz Heinrich Trithen worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and Karl Lachmann at Berlin. He held posts at the British Museum (1844–1848), Rugby School (~1844–1848), and as Professor of Modern Languages at Oxford (~1848–1851).

Franz Hessler was an Indology scholar who completed his Ph.D. while studying at Heidelberg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Würzburg between 1822 and 1827. In 1852, he was appointed an ordinary member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Franz Josef Meier was a scholar in Indology and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1925–1931). He served as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library from 1937 to 1970.

Franz Joseph Steingass worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earning his Ph.D. at Munich (~1843–1846). He taught at Wakefield Grammar School and was Professor of Modern Languages and Arabic lecturer at the Oriental Institute, Woking (~1889–1898).

Franz Karl Alter was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Charles University and the University of Vienna, where he also studied under Paulinus of St. Bartholomew. He worked at the Vienna University Library (1779) and the University of Vienna (~1781–1804).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey, earning his Ph.D. at Leipzig (1862). He served at Deccan College (1866–1881) and held the Chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen from 1881.

Franz Misteli was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Zurich, Bonn, Geneva, and Paris. He served as Privatdozent at the University of Bern in 1873, before becoming Professor of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Basel (1874; 1877–1898).

Franz Nikolaus Finck was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Marburg (~1893–1895). He held posts at the University of Marburg (PD, 1896), the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1903–1910), and Humboldt University of Berlin (PD 1903; ao. Professor 1909).

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin, completing his habilitation in 1829. He served there as Privatdozent (1829) and as an associate professor of theology from 1831.

Linguist Franz Specht earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig, studying under Ernst Windisch, August Leskien, Karl Brugmann, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at Halle (1923–1937), Halle-Wittenberg (~1926–1937), Breslau (1937–1943), Humboldt University of Berlin (1943–1945), and Mainz (1946–1949).

Franz Valéry Marie Cumont was a scholar of religious studies, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Charles Michel at Ghent University (Ph.D. ~1884–1887), where he subsequently served as a teacher (1892) and professor (1906).
